verbs.name: assets.providers
verbs.description: List the pluggable ASSET PROVIDERS — permission-scoped sources the agent/UI can SEARCH + FETCH media from, imported as normal project assets with the LICENSE + ATTRIBUTION surfaced (the first cut of the tool/plugin API). Each entry is {name, kinds, needs_key, network, note}. Pure READ (no project needed). The server-declared catalog is local_folder (a user-designated folder, filename search, no network — pass `dir` to assets.search; the hit id is the absolute path), openverse (api.openverse.org Creative-Commons media aggregator over Freesound/Jamendo/Wikimedia; keyless but rate-limited; commercial-use results), archive_org (Internet Archive public-domain/CC video and audio), wikimedia (Wikimedia Commons public-domain/CC media), nasa (NASA public-domain image and video), and stickers (offline built-in shape stickers). Network providers are contacted only when assets.search or assets.fetch is invoked; local_folder and stickers make no network request.

verbs.name: assets.search
verbs.description: Search an asset PROVIDER for media. Stateless — no project needed. Returns normalized hits the caller can preview + credit, then pass an id to assets.fetch. openverse hits are Creative-Commons (commercial-use filtered); local_folder hits are files under `dir` whose name contains `q`. The blocking network/fs work runs off the async runtime.

provider.description: Which provider to search (list them with assets.providers).

q.description: Search query (e.g. 'whoosh', 'rain', 'applause'). For local_folder this is a filename substring (empty = list all matching the kind).

kind.description: Media kind (default audio). openverse supports audio + image; local_folder supports all three.

dir.description: local_folder ONLY: the absolute folder path to search (required for that provider; ignored for openverse).

verbs.result: {provider, kind, count, hits: [{provider, id, title, kind, creator, license, license_url, source_url, download_url, filetype, duration_ms, filesize, attribution, requires_attribution}]}

verbs.name: assets.fetch
verbs.description: Import an asset-provider HIT as a normal project asset. Requires an OPEN project (the asset lands in it). Pass the `provider` + the `id` from a prior assets.search; the verb RE-RESOLVES the hit through the provider (no caller-supplied URL — no SSRF surface), then local_folder imports the file in place only when the id is still under the original search `dir`, while network providers DOWNLOAD it (size-capped, into the project's assets/providers/ dir). Import goes through the normal media-import chain (probe→proxy→filmstrip; receipts/replay intact), so the fetched asset is immediately usable on a track. The LICENSE + ATTRIBUTION are recorded on the import op and returned so the caller can credit the source (requires_attribution is false for CC0 / public-domain / local files).

provider.description: The provider the id came from (assets.search).

id.description: The hit id from assets.search (an Openverse uuid, or an absolute file path for local_folder).

kind.description: The hit's media kind (default audio) — must match the search kind so the provider resolves the right endpoint.

dir.description: local_folder ONLY: the same folder path passed to assets.search; fetch rejects local hits outside this folder.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {asset_id, job_id, provider, title, license, license_url, attribution, requires_attribution, source_url, op}; lowers to a media import op
